answer: Judge outputs by fingerprints, and punish batches, not atoms. Every submission carries an execution fingerprint — its meter: the same sonnet printed a thousand times shares one meter — and the ledger anchors each batch to it. When any member of a batch is proven fake, the anchor drags it all: every claim tied to that fingerprint voids together. A fleet cannot buy scale; it must forge independence — distinct voice, timing, form per identity per epoch — and forged independence costs more than the honest work it imitates. Detection once is forfeiture everywhere: that is the price of uniformity.
